slides.headline: Who is the painter? And why did Hitler want this painting?
slides.sub: Johannes Vermeer, The Art of Painting, about 1666-68

slides.headline: The curtain
slides.text: A heavy curtain is pulled back, as if we are secretly stepping into an artist's studio in Delft. Someone is at work.

slides.headline: The painter
slides.text: The painter sits with his back to us, in a smart black doublet. We never see his face. Could it be Vermeer?

slides.headline: The model
slides.text: His model holds a trumpet and a book, crowned with laurel. She is dressed as Clio, the muse of history.

slides.headline: The map
slides.text: On the wall hangs a huge map of the Netherlands, with a crease running across it, as if the country were split in two.

slides.headline: The mask
slides.text: On the table, a mask lies beside the books and fabric. Painting, Vermeer seems to say, is about fame and memory.

slides.headline: Never sold
slides.text: Vermeer never sold this painting. After he was gone, his widow tried hard to keep it away from his creditors.

slides.headline: Hitler
slides.text: Centuries later, Adolf Hitler bought it for his planned museum. After the war it was found hidden in an Austrian salt mine.

slides.headline: Who is he?
slides.text: We never see the painter's face. Do you think Vermeer painted himself, or only the idea of a painter?
